Norovirus Outbreak Disrupts Swedish Renewable Energy Sites

A norovirus outbreak has disrupted operations at multiple renewable energy facilities across Sweden, with battery manufacturer NorthVolt AB among the affected companies. The outbreak, which began late last week at a cluster of sites in Västerbotten and Västernorrland counties, has led to temporary workforce shortages and delays in ongoing projects.

According to the Swedish Renewable Energy Association, more than 120 workers have reported symptoms consistent with norovirus infection, including severe gastrointestinal distress. “We’re seeing significant absenteeism at several plants,” said Association spokesperson Karin Lund. “Site managers are balancing the need to maintain output with the health and safety of their teams.”

NorthVolt AB, operator of Sweden’s largest battery manufacturing facility, confirmed that production lines have been forced to reduce capacity as a result of the outbreak. “We have implemented enhanced hygiene protocols and deep cleaning procedures,” said NorthVolt AB communications manager Johan Nilsson. “Our priority is to support affected employees and limit further spread, but there has been an unavoidable impact on production targets this week.”

Local health authorities are investigating the source of the outbreak, which is suspected to be linked to a shared onsite canteen frequently used by contract workers at multiple facilities, including those operated by NorthVolt AB and the wind turbine component firm Svea Windworks. “We’re working closely with companies to isolate cases and minimize further disruption,” said Dr. Maria Ekström, Västerbotten County’s chief medical officer.

Industry analysts warn that even brief interruptions could have knock-on effects for project timelines. “Given the tight schedules in the sector, a week-long slowdown can set some projects back by months,” said Jakob Persson, an energy sector consultant. “The full impact won’t be clear until the outbreak is contained.”

As of Tuesday, several sites remain partially staffed, and authorities have not yet declared the outbreak over.
